facts.text: Roseland takes its name from 18th‑century pastor Robert Rose, who owned land there and chronicled his travels through the area.
The community sits in the Blue Ridge foothills, where the terrain slopes from 600 to 1,000 feet and shapes local rivers and valleys.
In August 1969, Roseland endured catastrophic flash flooding when Hurricane Camille dumped up to 27 inches of rain in just two days.
Roseland is a stop on Virginia’s Craft Beverage Trail, home to Devil’s Backbone Brewing, Blue Toad Hard Cider, and Bryant’s Small Batch Cider.
Before European settlement, the Monacan Indian Nation farmed and hunted in the fertile valleys that now surround Roseland.
The town’s elevation ranges between 600 and 1,000 feet, giving it rolling hills, steep forested slopes, and open agricultural valleys.
